advisor_identified: Historian of early America and professor of history at Morgan State University.

doctorate.title: To 'Encourage and Protect' American Manufactures: The Intellectual Origins of Industrialization, 1763-1830

evidence.says: Morgan State identifies Lawrence Peskin as a professor in History and Geography specializing in early America, and lists his PhD in History from the University of Maryland, College Park.

Richard S. Chew, Unforeseen Troubles: Baltimore's Atlantic Trade and the Commercial Frustrations of the Confederation Period, p. 28, note 36, cites Lawrence Peskin's To 'Encourage and Protect' American Manufactures: The Intellectual Origins of Industrialization, 1763-1830 as a University of Maryland, College Park PhD dissertation, 1998.
The graduate handbook identifies Lawrence Peskin as coordinator of graduate programs and a graduate faculty member in history, with a PhD from the University of Maryland, College Park.

notes: The linked dissertation matches the independently cited author, institution, year and title. The faculty page confirms the degree and institution; the year and title are established through a scholarly dissertation citation rather than a thesis catalogue record.
